title: April-May rain had a negative link to Orange-tip flight-period balance in England in 2005-2024
abstract: We tested whether April-May rain was linked to the balance of the recorded Orange-tip flight period. Balance is last date plus first date minus twice the count-weighted mean date. Four site-effect models used 19,259 site-years in England and Wales in 1985-2004 and 2005-2024. Models controlled spring and winter temperature, time and peak count. Each year had equal total weight. The later English slope was -1.95 days per 100 mm, with a four-test adjusted 95 percent interval of -3.70 to -0.20. The other three intervals included zero. Count, season and site filters kept the later English estimate negative. A following-year weather check gave an interval across zero. Thus, a clear link did not repeat across regions and periods. Missing visits, survey limits, selected sites, coarse weather and 20 annual exposures per main fit limit inference. This is a seasonal association, not a causal climate or pollution effect. The package gives code, exact source hashes, aggregate results and a figure. External source and record-level data remain outside the bundle.
